extracted.intended_audience: crisis managers, emergency planners, public-sector leaders, and organizational executives
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for designing, operating, and evaluating organizational and public-sector crisis management plans, communication, leadership, and inter-agency coordination across all crisis phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-cultural communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate cross-cultural communication in crisis management plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/anti-patterns: The Bhopal disaster illustrates the danger of poor communication—operating manuals printed only in English prevented local residents from understanding warnings. Ensure warnings, manuals and messaging are linguistically and culturally accessible to local populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, consistent management plan for multi-national operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a clear management plan that consistently applies management standards across multinational operations to avoid blame-shifting and mismanagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Bhopal demonstrated difficulty in consistently applying management standards and resulted in blame shifting when a clear plan was absent. Guidance: define roles, decision authority, and escalation procedures across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early responsibility and transparent communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond early with transparent, factual communication rather than deflecting blame or remaining silent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/anti-patterns: Ford/Firestone's initial responses blamed consumers and each other and delayed describing corrective actions; these were major blunders. Guidance: avoid blaming others, state what is known, what is being done, and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive media engagement and executive involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage proactively with media and public; involve senior executives in communications efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Exxon did not react quickly to media/public and the CEO shunned public involvement, harming the response. Guidance: appoint spokespeople, ensure CEO or senior leader visible when appropriate, establish a media center suitable for expected media volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated communications team and capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a communications plan and a communications team (including a PR/communications manager) before a crisis occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Exxon had no communications team and did not appoint a public relations manager until years later. Guidance: pre-designate communications leadership, templates, contact lists, and physical/virtual media infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective consequence management to protect shareholder value
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage the consequences of catastrophes effectively to reduce long-term negative impact on shareholder value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research (Knight & Pretty) shows that organizations that effectively manage consequences may recover or exceed pre-catastrophe stock price. Guidance: use crisis response to preserve financial and reputational assets; engage senior management in valuing crisis management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt crisis-as-opportunity mindset (crisis leadership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Move from managing crisis reactively to using crises to showcase institutional character and generate leadership and improvement opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hilburg and other sources argue every crisis can showcase commitment to brand and values. Guidance: immediately address damage and implications, seek opportunities for reform and improvement while balancing accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership competencies under pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure leaders have competencies to perform under pressure and guide the organization through crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research shows leaders who perform well under pressure guide the organization effectively. Guidance: develop training, selection and development programs linking crisis management and leadership competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage beyond communications—operational response matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that reputation damage can result from the actual management of the issue, so actions (not just PR) must address operational and strategic problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James notes executives focus on communications reactively; however, the company's reputation and survival depend on substantive management of the crisis, not only messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-reliance on statistical significance for crisis determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not let risk-management groups delay action by debating whether an event is 'statistically significant'; make timely decisions about when to treat an incident as a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: establish threshold criteria and decision rules that allow timely escalation rather than paralysis by statistical debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover all crisis phases (incubation, onset, aftermath)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis leadership must concern itself with all phases of a crisis: incubation stage, onset, and aftermath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: planning, detection, immediate response, recovery and post-crisis learning should all be addressed in plans and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis leadership five critical tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis leadership involves five critical tasks: sense making, decision making, meaning making, terminating, and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief descriptions from the page: Sense making = situation assessment; Decision making = choosing and implementing actions; Meaning making = political communication/interpretation; Terminating = handling accountability to end the crisis; Learning = using the crisis to reform though learning may be limited. Use this as a framework for leader roles and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive incident coverage in plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis-management plans should cover a wide variety of incidents (e.g., bomb threats, child abuse, natural disasters, suicide, drug abuse, gang activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: develop scenario-based plans and checklists for the full range of plausible incidents relevant to the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience/stakeholder-tailored communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans should address all audiences in need of information including parents, the media and law enforcement officials (and other stakeholders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: map stakeholder groups, tailor messages and channels, and predefine roles for communicating with each audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a unified incident management framework and chain-of-command
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate public and private response by providing a common language and outlining a chain-of-command when multiple parties are mobilized (e.g., National Response Plan concept).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NRP premise: handle incidents at the lowest organizational level possible; provide common language and chain-of-command. Guidance: adopt or align with national/regional incident management systems to ensure interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate private sector as key partner
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and integrate the private sector as a key partner in domestic incident management, particularly for critical infrastructure protection and restoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: build public-private coordination mechanisms, liaison roles, and information-sharing protocols with private stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standardized alerting protocols and multi-modal alerts (CAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ mechanisms like the Common Alerting Protocol to facilitate crisis communication across different mediums and systems and to reach geographically and linguistically diverse audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAP helps create a consistent emergency alert format for audio and visual media. Guidance: adopt standards so alerts are interoperable across systems and media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate across government levels and emergency services
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify roles and coordination among local, state, national government, emergency services, and national guard in crisis response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: establish protocols that specify responsibilities across levels of government and among emergency service providers to avoid gaps or duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide crisis/emergency training to increase staff knowledge and self-efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver emergency and crisis training across institutions to improve staff knowledge and confidence in responding to crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence: studies found higher staff knowledge correlated with higher self-efficacy. Training resources: FEMA Emergency Management Institute, web-based courses. Guidance: regular training and exercises to build capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance centralization and decentralization appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Design governance to balance central control and regional autonomy; decentralization can allow flexibility but may hinder coordinated response during large-scale crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Italy and Spain faced coordination problems due to decentralized health management during COVID-19; Iran used central control with local flexibility. Guidance: define integration mechanisms to reconcile autonomy with national objectives in systemic crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate legislation and instruments into structural frameworks for systemic crises
rubrics_metrics.description: Update and integrate existing and future legislation and instruments into a framework capable of dealing structurally with increasingly systemic and large-scale crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation (SAPEA): align legal and institutional instruments within a resilience and preparedness framework. Guidance: review statutory powers, mandates and inter-agency agreements to ensure they support systemic crisis response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage citizen-focused approaches and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop citizen-focused approaches that encourage engagement and compliance, and build domestic capacity (e.g., domestic production of supplies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Iran's citizen-focused approach and domestic production of medical supplies aided its COVID-19 response. Guidance: include behavioral economics, public information campaigns, and strategies to motivate public cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align with professional standards and industry associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use guidance, certifications, and best practices from professional organizations (e.g., ASIS, DRI, Turnaround Management Association, ISO/TC 223).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: adopt recognized standards, training and certification programs to professionalize crisis and continuity management and ensure consistency with industry practices.
